newsitem.title: USA: Brad Pitt sues to cover up nude photographs.
newsitem.headline: Brad Pitt sues to cover up nude photographs.

text.p: A judge on Monday ordered Playgirl magazine not to deliver any more copies of its August edition that contain photographs of movie star Brad Pitt in the nude.
However, Judge Robert O'Brien did not order the magazine's recall, as Pitt had demanded.
In his suit filed in Los Angeles Superior Court, Pitt sought an injunction against the magazine.

He said that the photographs were taken in 1995 by a photographer who trespassed on the grounds of a hotel in the West Indies to shoot in a bungalow where Pitt was staying with his then girlfriend Gwyneth Paltrow. Paltrow appears in some of the photos.
O'Brien sealed the file, but Playgirl lawyer Kent Raygor said the judge only approved half of Pitt's request.
"The magazine is not to be distributed, but we are not required to recall it," Raygor told reporters outside the court.
The August issue of the magazine, with the headline "Brad Pitt Nude", hit the newsstands on Monday but subscription issues had already been sent out.
The judge scheduled a hearing for July 29 to decide if he will extend the order.
The screen heartthrob, referred to by his full name of William Bradley Pitt in his suit, wants unspecified damages for invasion of privacy and infliction of emotional distress.
His lawyer John Lavely told the judge that Pitt had been assured of his privacy while vacationing at the hotel on the French West Indies island of Saint Barthelemy.
However, Playgirl's lawyer Raygor argued the pictures are two years old, and have already been published in European publications and were available on the Internet.
He said he did not know how the magazine got hold of the photographs.
